claim: Law-firm commentary (Foley, April 2026): most US state comprehensive privacy laws define consumer narrowly, so commercial/employment-context individuals, B2B contacts, employees and applicants are generally excluded.
quote: individuals acting in a commercial or employment context are generally excluded from coverage. As a result, business-to-business contacts, employees, and job applicants typically fall outside the scope of these statutes
title: Foley: The Compliance Tightrope (commentary)

claim: Foley (April 2026) states California still applies its law to personal information of employees, applicants, contractors and business contacts residing in California, i.e. remains the exception.
quote: California takes a broader approach, applying its law to personal information collected from or about employees, job applicants, independent contractors, and business representatives and contacts who reside in that State.
title: Foley: The Compliance Tightrope (commentary)

claim: GDPR Art. 3(2) applies to processing by a controller or processor not established in the Union when it relates to offering goods or services to, or monitoring behaviour of, data subjects in the Union.
quote: the monitoring of their behaviour as far as their behaviour takes place within the Union.
title: GDPR Article 3 (text, gdpr-info.eu reproduction of Regulation 2016/679)
